IS-IS.fact: Intermediate System to Intermediate System (IS-IS, also written ISIS) is a link-state interior gateway protocol (IGP), typically deployed within a single autonomous system, and is used in large enterprise and service provider networks to exchange routing information. IS-IS.fact: In this example LSP with ID 1921.6820.0002.02-01, 1921.6820.0002 is the System ID (that generated this LSP), 02 is the Pseudonode ID, 01 is the Fragment ID. If an LSP exceeds the maximum transmission unit (MTU), it is fragmented into multiple LSPs distinguished by a Fragment ID.

IS-IS.question: While not required by the protocol, a common operational practice is to set the _____ ID field to a unique IPv4 address from one of the router’s loopback interfaces

While not required by the protocol, a common operational practice is to set the System ID field to a unique IPv4 address from one of the router’s loopback interfaces.

IS-IS.fact: While not required by the protocol, a common operational practice is to set the System ID field to a unique IPv4 address from one of the router’s loopback interfaces. On a single intermediate system there can be up to 3 NET addresses.

IS-IS.fact: Area itself consists of an AFI (Address Family Identifier) and an Area ID.

IS-IS.fact: The NET consists of an Area, System ID and NSEL field. The System ID is six bytes long and the NSEL is one byte.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: As an example, the fields of the ISO Network Address "49.0100._____.6821.1138.00" are as follows: 49 is the AFI
IS-IS.fact: As an example, the fields of the ISO Network Address "49.0100.1921.6821.1138.00" are as follows: 49 is the AFI. 49 specifically represents the "private address space", similar to RFC1918 for IPv4., 0100 is the Area ID, 49.0100 is the Area, 1921.6821.1138 is the System ID, 00 is the NSEL, which must be zero.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: 49 specifically represents the "private address space", similar to RFC1918 for IPv4., 0100 is the Area ID, 49.0100 is the Area, _____.6821.1138 is the System ID, 00 is the NSEL, which must be zero
IS-IS.fact: As an example, the fields of the ISO Network Address "49.0100.1921.6821.1138.00" are as follows: 49 is the AFI. 49 specifically represents the "private address space", similar to RFC1918 for IPv4., 0100 is the Area ID, 49.0100 is the Area, 1921.6821.1138 is the System ID, 00 is the NSEL, which must be zero.

IS-IS.question: Level 1 routers are internal to an area, and only maintain a _____ (LSDB) for that area
IS-IS.fact: Level 1 routers are internal to an area, and only maintain a Link State Database (LSDB) for that area.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: They maintain a separate _____ 2 LSDB for inter-area routing
IS-IS.fact: In IS-IS, ISs operate at Level 1, Level 2 or Level 1/Level 2. Level 1 routers are internal to an area, and only maintain a Link State Database (LSDB) for that area.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: When a _____ 1 router needs to send traffic to a destination not within its area, it directs it to a Level 1/Level 2 router
IS-IS.fact: They maintain a separate Level 2 LSDB for inter-area routing. Level 2 routers must be contiguous, meaning the network of Level 2 routers must be fully internally routable without crossing into different areas.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: Level 1/Level 2 routers advertise their status as boundary routers by setting the _____ (ATT), in its Level 1 LSP
IS-IS.fact: Level 1/Level 2 routers advertise their status as boundary routers by setting the Attached Bit (ATT), in its Level 1 LSP.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: External routes may be redistributed into _____ 1 areas via Level 1/Level 2 routers
IS-IS.fact: When a Level 1 router needs to send traffic to a destination not within its area, it directs it to a Level 1/Level 2 router. Level 1/Level 2 routers advertise their status as boundary routers by setting the Attached Bit (ATT), in its Level 1 LSP.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: By default, external routes are not advertised into the _____ 2 backbone; redistribution into Level 2 must be explicitly configured on Level 1/Level 2 routers
IS-IS.fact: Level 1/Level 2 routers advertise their status as boundary routers by setting the Attached Bit (ATT), in its Level 1 LSP. External routes may be redistributed into Level 1 areas via Level 1/Level 2 routers.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: P bit – _____ repair bit, 8th bit, indicates if a partitioned Level 1 area can be repaired (joined) over Level 2 area
IS-IS.fact: P bit – Partition repair bit, 8th bit, indicates if a partitioned Level 1 area can be repaired (joined) over Level 2 area. Modern deployments of IS-IS generally do not support partition repair, and will not set the P bit.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: ATT bit – _____ bit, 7th–4th bits, indicates if the originating router is attached to another area
IS-IS.fact: ATT bit – Attached bit, 7th–4th bits, indicates if the originating router is attached to another area.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: If these bits are set by the _____ 1/Level 2 router in its Level 1 LSP, other routers in the Level 1 area will automatically generate a default route to the originator
IS-IS.fact: P bit – Partition repair bit, 8th bit, indicates if a partitioned Level 1 area can be repaired (joined) over Level 2 area. If these bits are set by the Level 1/Level 2 router in its Level 1 LSP, other routers in the Level 1 area will automatically generate a default route to the originator.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: There are 4 ATT bits which represent the Error, _____, Delay and Default metrics respectively
IS-IS.fact: There are 4 ATT bits which represent the Error, Expense, Delay and Default metrics respectively.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: OL bit – _____ bit, 3rd bit, indicates if the router is overloaded
IS-IS.fact: OL bit – Overload bit, 3rd bit, indicates if the router is overloaded. The overload bit can be set automatically by a router under heavy load or intentionally by an administrator.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: When BGP is finished establishing neighborship, the overload bit is cleared and this router joins the _____ VPN
IS-IS.fact: An example of this behavior is a provider edge router running an MPLS VPN with IS-IS and BGP. When BGP is finished establishing neighborship, the overload bit is cleared and this router joins the MPLS VPN.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: It can be _____ 1 only, Level 2 only, or Level 1/Level 2
IS-IS.fact: It can be Level 1 only, Level 2 only, or Level 1/Level 2.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: An elected DIS router is a pseudonode, which uses the resources (including _____ ID) of one real router
IS-IS.fact: In order to overcome this issue, on each LAN segment a designated intermediate system (DIS) is elected. The router with the highest priority and System ID is elected as the DIS, but if another router is connected with a higher priority (or higher System ID if the priorities are equal), it will be elected as the new DIS.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: LSPs originated by a DIS always have a non-zero _____ ID field
IS-IS.fact: An elected DIS router is a pseudonode, which uses the resources (including System ID) of one real router. LSPs originated by a DIS always have a non-zero Pseudonode ID field.

IS-IS.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
IS-IS.question: Authentication may be configured on a per-interface and per-level (_____ 1 or Level 2) basis
